finding_site:src/ici/analysis/_clazy.py:.comparison: Frozen legacy LintEngine C++ heuristic fallback (no compilation database; `ici lint` has no analysis context at all): per-source g++ text diagnostics become `Compiler:<-W rule>` or `C++Syntax` targets with '<kind>: <message>' (errors FAIL; warnings, notes, remarks WARN; each note its own C++Syntax target after its parent), a clean source becomes `C++Syntax:fallback` PASS 'Compiler syntax analysis completed without diagnostics.', ClangTidyUnavailable/ClazyUnavailable targets follow at '.', and the summary is '0 Violations Found' / the first two tool warnings when nothing failed / '<F> Errors, <W> Warnings Found' (W counts WARN targets plus the fallback tool warning). Rust's legacy projection (crate::cpp::legacy_fallback_lint over the cpp.diagnostics fallback output and crate::cpp::legacy_tooling_unavailable for cpp.tidy, execute.rs/cpp.rs) matches all 5 oracle cases exactly (targets in order, summary, status, evidence, exit 1 for errors and exit 0 for warnings only). This site: ClazyUnavailable at '.', WARN by default and ERROR (summary = the message, exit 1) with clazy='required'. With resolvable tools on an exact context: the clean-run `<Tool>:<digest>` PASS, `<Tool>ContextMissing` ERROR and the second tool's Unavailable target now match frozen (lint-oracle.json tool_cases). Rust's legacy cpp.tidy projection (crate::cpp::legacy_tooling) turns each native clang-tidy/clazy provider run on a recorded unit into the frozen targets: a clean run is `ClangTidy:<compile_db configuration digest[:12]>` / `Clazy:<digest>` PASS '<tool> completed without diagnostics.' at the source, each primary diagnostic `ClangTidy:<check>` / `ClangAnalyzer:<clang-analyzer-*>` / `Clazy:clazy-<check>` with '<kind>: <message>' at its line and column (errors FAIL, otherwise WARN), a failed run `<Tool>ExecutionError` ERROR with the frozen _process_error text; the clang-tidy block (or ClangTidyUnavailable) precedes the clazy block (or ClazyUnavailable), a tool that ran reports each production source without a recorded command as `<Tool>ContextMissing` ERROR before its runs, and an unresolvable second tool keeps its Unavailable WARN target and estimated evidence. The frozen LintEngine verdict (crate::cpp::legacy_lint_verdict) is recomputed over the syntax and tooling targets once the tooling ran: '0 Violations Found', the first two tool warnings, '<F> Errors, <W> Warnings Found', or the joined tool errors. All 5 comparable cases match exactly.
